claims.text: GDACS assessed Tropical Cyclone NOUL-26 (Kiyapo) at an Orange alert level, indicating medium humanitarian impact, for an event affecting China and the Philippines between 23 and 26 July 2026, with about 11.9 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds.

GDACS recorded maximum sustained winds of 157 km/h (Category 2 equivalent, per JTWC data) for Tropical Cyclone NOUL-26, with a maximum storm surge of 1.6 metres occurring on 25 July 2026 at 21:00 UTC; as of 25 July the storm centre was located about 135 km east of Catanduanes, Philippines.

GDACS's event report for Tropical Cyclone NOUL-26 (eventid 1001294) shows the event time window closed at 23 Jul 2026 06:00 UTC to 26 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC, with the alert urgency status now "Past" and no episode updates since — the maximum sustained wind (157 km/h), 11.9 million population exposure, and 1.6 m storm surge figures are unchanged from the 26 July assessment.

description: Tropical Cyclone NOUL-26 (named Kiyapo in the Philippines, Hongxia in China) tracked across the northern Philippines and the South China Sea in late July 2026 before making a second landfall in Guangdong province, southern China, around 26 July 2026. GDACS assessed an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, with about 11.9 million people exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds across the Philippines and China, maximum sustained winds of 157 km/h (Category 2 equivalent, per JTWC data), and a maximum storm surge of 1.6 metres recorded on 25 July 2026. GDACS's event window closed at 00:00 UTC on 26 July 2026 with the alert's urgency status marked "Past" and no episode updates since; no authoritative source published a confirmed death toll, injury count, or evacuation figure for this storm, and with the cyclone dissipated and no further GDACS activity for five days, the event is assessed as resolved.
